column12: issue #58 and f317753971, which walks the sibling tree in order; MS-OXMSG 2.2.2 numbers attachment storages __attach_version1.0_#XXXXXXXX, so they must come back in index order whatever shape the red-black tree has

column4: A stream in regular sectors was read contiguously from its first sector, ignoring its FAT chain
column12: 9908c12cca (test2/Normal.bin, a stream whose sectors are out of order; likely issues #23 and #36, files that failed after Outlook rewrote them); MS-CFB 2.3: a stream's sectors are found by following the FAT chain, here stored in reverse physical order

column4: A Uint8Array that is a view into a larger buffer was read from the start of the whole buffer
column12: 9908c12cca (DataStream ignored the byte offset of Node's pooled Buffers). Bodu's analog is a MemoryStream over a segment of a larger array: copy gen:Msg(0037001F=Segment) into an array at offset 1024 between filler bytes, open MemoryStream(array, 1024, length, writable: false, publiclyVisible: true) with OutlookMessage.Open, and Subject must be "Segment"

column12: issue #35 and 18cd9bbe9a, which returns an empty array for a zero-length stream instead of reading its start sector; MS-CFB 2.6.3: a stream of size 0 has no sectors, so the subject and the attachment data are empty

column4: The mini FAT was read before the DIFAT, so a file whose mini FAT is reached only through the DIFAT failed
column12: issue #20 (a message attaching a big message threw) and 5321f76604; MS-CFB 2.5: FAT sectors past the first 109 are listed in DIFAT sectors; the 7,500,000-byte attachment needs 116 FAT sectors, and the mini FAT is moved to a sector whose FAT entry lies in one of them, so the subject (in the mini stream) needs the DIFAT

column4: The compound-file reader crashed on chains and directory entries that run past the end of the data; sanity checks now stop there
column12: 499ced1eeb (from markb-trustifi) stops at a FAT entry, mini FAT link or directory entry beyond the data; Bodu rejects a malformed container, here one whose last sector (its FAT) is cut off, with CompoundFileFormatException at the Compatible and Strict levels (docs/docs/io-compound/concepts.md:89), which OutlookMessage.Open wraps in OutlookMsgFormatException (its XML documentation)

column4: The named-property storage was read as message fields, so its name-to-ID mapping stream __substg1.0_10000102 replaced the body
column12: 62e74fc9d8 skips __nameid_version1.0 when reading fields; MS-OXMSG 2.2.3.2: the mapping storage holds name-to-ID streams named __substg1.0_10XX0102 (0x1000 here, for LID 0x801A in PS_PUBLIC_STRINGS), which are not properties of the message, so PidTagBody stays the root's value
